chunks: Indeed, Allah, Glorified is He, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a warner for the worlds, and a witness over the messengers. When he passed away (peace be upon him), the Muslims quarreled over the matter (of leadership) after him.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the dispute over leadership after the Prophet's death in his letter to Malik al-Ashtar?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) opens this seminal administrative letter by establishing the theological foundation of Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) dual role as a warner and a witness over previous messengers. He then highlights the immediate post-prophetic dispute over authority, a key event in Shia historiography that underscores the necessity of just governance derived from divine mandate rather than mere political consensus.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Allāh the Glorified, deputed Muḥammad (may Allāh bless him and his descendants) as a warner for all the worlds and a witness for all the prophets. When the Prophet expired, the Muslims quarreled about power after him.
